cards.explanation: The answer is food and water. Moses says the Ammonites and Moabites "…did not meet you with food and water on your way out of Egypt…" (Deuteronomy 23:4). Think of a long road trip where nobody hands you so much as a cup of water, friends. That sticks with you.

The answer is Balaam son of Beor. Moses says they hired "…Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Aram-naharaim to curse you." (Deuteronomy 23:4). Notice they hired him. They paid somebody to do the cursing. I've had a worn-out stamper's bad days, friends, but nobody ever hired a guy against me.

The answer is blessing. Moses says, "…the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you…" (Deuteronomy 23:5). Balaam was hired to curse Israel. What the verse says came out for Israel was a blessing. Curse in, blessing out, friends.

The answer is that the LORD loves them. The verse gives the reason itself: "…because the LORD your God loves you." (Deuteronomy 23:5). That is the reason the text gives. Short and sweet, and it's plenty, friends.
The answer is brother. Moses says, "Do not despise an Edomite, for he is your brother." (Deuteronomy 23:7). Edom's family tie to Israel is the reason given. You don't look down on family, friends.

The answer is True. Moses says, "Do not despise an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land." (Deuteronomy 23:7). Israel knew what it was to be the outsider living somewhere else. That's the reason he gives, friends.

The answer is the third generation. Moses says, "The third generation of children born to them may enter the assembly of the LORD." (Deuteronomy 23:8). He's talking about Edomites and Egyptians. Just before it, he says an Edomite is a brother and that Israel lived as a foreigner in Egypt (Deuteronomy 23:7).

The answer is after washing when the sun sets. Moses says, "When evening approaches, he must wash with water, and when the sun sets he may return to the camp." (Deuteronomy 23:11). One wash and one sunset, and he's back inside. No waiting around for days, friends.

The answer is that He protects them and hands over their enemies. Moses says the LORD "…walks throughout your camp to protect you and deliver your enemies to you." (Deuteronomy 23:14). He isn't watching from far away. He's walking right through the middle of the camp, friends.

The answer is False. Moses says, "Your camp must be holy, lest He see anything unclean among you and turn away from you." (Deuteronomy 23:14). So the LORD turning away is the warning, not a promise to stay no matter what. That's a serious warning, friends, and it's why the camp had to be kept clean.
The answer is False. Moses says, "Do not return a slave to his master if he has taken refuge with you." (Deuteronomy 23:15). A slave who runs to Israel for refuge isn't sent back, friends.

The answer is in whatever town he chooses. Moses says, "Let him live among you wherever he chooses, in the town of his pleasing." (Deuteronomy 23:16). The choice is his. Right before that, Moses says not to return a slave to his master if he has taken refuge with you (Deuteronomy 23:15).

The answer is False. Moses says, "You must not bring the wages of a prostitute, whether female or male, into the house of the LORD your God to fulfill any vow…" (Deuteronomy 23:18). Those wages stay out. The verse gives the reason: "…both are detestable to the LORD your God."

The answer is that both are detestable to the LORD. These wages can't come in "…because both are detestable to the LORD your God." (Deuteronomy 23:18). The reason comes from the LORD Himself, and it's a serious one, friends.

The answer is a foreigner. Moses says, "You may charge a foreigner interest, but not your brother…" (Deuteronomy 23:20). The line is drawn between a brother and a foreigner. He ties it to a blessing on everything they put their hand to in the land.

The answer is bless. Moses says the point is "…so that the LORD your God may bless you in everything to which you put your hand in the land that you are entering to possess." (Deuteronomy 23:20). Bless is the word, friends, and it covers everything they put their hand to.

The answer is that He will surely require it. Moses says, "…do not be slow to keep it, because He will surely require it of you, and you will be guilty of sin." (Deuteronomy 23:21). The LORD takes a vow seriously, so a vow is not a small thing to say, friends.
The answer is True. Moses says, "…if you refrain from making a vow, you will not be guilty of sin." (Deuteronomy 23:22). Nobody has to make a vow. Skipping one is no sin, friends.

The answer is eat your fill of grapes. Moses says, "…you may eat your fill of grapes…" (Deuteronomy 23:24). That's generous. You walk in and eat until you've had enough. But hold that thought, friends, because the basket comes up in the very same verse.

The answer is False. Moses says you may eat your fill of grapes, but you "…must not put any in your basket." (Deuteronomy 23:24). Eat all you want, right there in the vineyard. The basket is where the answer turns into NO. I've had a few cookies in my day that I stuffed in my apron when nobody was looking, so I know that basket feeling, friends.

The answer is sickle. Moses says you may pluck the heads of grain with your hand, but "…you must not put a sickle to your neighbor’s grain." (Deuteronomy 23:25). Hand is allowed. Sickle is the line. One word, big difference, friends.
